title: LEX v1.6.0: a new large-eddy simulation model in JAX with GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation
parameterization_target: Subgrid-scale (SGS) corrections for potential temperature, water vapor mixing ratio, and velocity components in the turbulence gray zone
code_availability: The current version of LEX is publicly available on Github at https://github.com/MetLab-HKUST/LEX (last access: 30 January 2026) under the MIT license. LEX codes, and scripts for producing figures are archived on Zenodo under https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15486687 (Zhu et al., 2025a).
testbed_rationale: Publicly provides high-fidelity LES benchmark simulation data alongside a fully auto-differentiable GPU-accelerated LES code (LEX in JAX) designed specifically for coupled online learning of subgrid-scale turbulence parameterizations.
pain_points: Long JIT compilation and setup overhead relative to short integration periods
Requirement of double precision (float64) during training to prevent rounding error instabilities, which slows execution and lacks native hardware convolution support on certain GPUs
Unphysical initial neural network predictions (e.g., negative water vapor mixing ratios and background noise), requiring custom penalties (non-negative loss and Laplacian pyramid loss)
Extreme sensitivity of differentiable multi-step rollouts to parameter initialization, necessitating staged curriculum training across 3, 6, and 12 look-ahead steps
Spatial domain parallelism is hindered by the iterative BiCGSTAB pressure solver, limiting current multi-device execution to batch-level parallelism
extraction_notes: LEX solves Durran's (2008) pseudo-incompressible acoustic-wave-filtered equations in JAX with SSPRK3 and WENO spatial discretization. The DL model predicts single-step SGS tendency corrections coupled online inside differentiable roll-out loops.
